newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ trade balance trend deteriorates in February.
newsitem.headline: NZ trade balance trend deteriorates in February.

text.p: The trend in the balance of New Zealand's merchandise trade has deteriorated over the last three months, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday.
The exports trend has now fallen 0.6 percent per month from November 1996, while the imports trend has fallen by an average of 0.2 percent per month over the same period.
The unadjusted value of exports for February was NZ$1.67 billion, down 3.6 percent from a year ago.

Unadjusted imports fell 10.2 percent over the same period to a value of $1.51 billion, with falls in mineral fuels, mechanical machinery, vehicles, pharmaceuticals and aircraft contributing significantly to the fall.
A trade surplus of $159.7 million was recorded in February, against a surplus of $50.6 million in February 1996.
An MMS Pacific survey showed a median forecast of a $75 million surplus for the month.
Unadjusted exports for the year to February rose 1.4 percent to $20.86 billion, with exports of dairy produce and mineral fuels contributing strongly to the rise.
Imports were valued at $21.17 billion, a fall of 1.9 percent from the February 1996 year. A fall in aircraft imports was a major contributor.
A trade deficit of $309.8 million was recorded for the February year, an improvement of $701 million from the deficit of $1.01 billion recorded for the February 1996 year.
If large irregular items such as ships and aircraft were excluded, the trade deficit for the February year would have been $204 million, and for the February 1996 year $683 million.
